title: OpenAI API Pricing 2026: Cost Per Model Compared
summary: OpenAI API pricing spans from $0.50 to $20 per million output tokens, a 40-fold variation that directly impacts your model selection decisions.
body_markdown:
## OpenAI API cost for 1,000 summaries and classifications


### The gap between the top and bottom tier


$15.50 buys a thousand email summaries on GPT-6 Astra, and the same thousand cost $0.155 on GPT-6 Luna, so the cheapest model does the same work for one hundredth of the money.


Take 800 input and 150 output tokens per summary and 400 and 20 per classification, priced from[OpenAI's pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) . The multiple's the same for both jobs, so a lighter task doesn't narrow the gap.


For summaries (800 input, 150 output tokens), $15.50 on GPT-6 Astra against $0.155 on GPT-6 Luna is a gap of $15.345, which means Astra costs roughly a hundred times more per summary.


For ticket classifications (400 input, 20 output), $5.00 against $0.05 is a gap of $4.95, making the expensive model a hundred times costlier per ticket. Both come to 100x.


Neither job needs the flagship, so the cheaper tiers below are where the saving sits.


### What mid-tier OpenAI models cost per task


The summary batch cost $3.10 on the earlier GPT-6 Sol, one fifth of Astra. GPT-5.6 Sol costs $6.20 and GPT-5.6 Terra $3.40, so the older models cost more than a newer Sol such as GPT-6.1 Sol.


GPT-5.6 Luna's $0.34, over twice GPT-6 Luna's $0.155, which means staying on an old cheap model still overpays.


For classification, a label's about 20 output tokens, so the bill's mostly input. On the earlier GPT-6 Sol the same batch cost $1.00, and a mid-tier model like GPT-6.1 Sol covers the job, so Astra's $5.00 is paying for capability this step doesn't need.


Run the same batch on GPT-5.6 Sol and it's $2.00; GPT-5.6 Terra is $1.04, GPT-5.6 Luna $0.104, and GPT-6 Luna $0.05. That means Luna costs a fortieth of what GPT-5.6 Sol does.


### OpenAI API cost at monthly volume


At 10,000 summaries a month, Astra costs $155 and Luna $1.55, making Astra a hundred times as expensive, which means you're burning $153.45 monthly for identical results. At 100,000, that becomes $1,550 against $15.50.


Run classifications instead and it's $50 and $0.50 at 10,000, then $500 and $5.00 at 100,000. The flagship choice's a four-figure monthly decision on one step.


A platform that bundles a model into its product has chosen your model and set its price before you log in.


Activepieces works the other way round: its OpenAI integration, one of 741 counted in its open source monorepo, runs on your own OpenAI key, so GPT-6 Luna's $0.50 per million output tokens is billed to your OpenAI account at your rate, not ours.


The model is a setting on each action, which means the strategy stays yours, and you can reach the same flows from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client; the[integration's page](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/openai) lists the actions it exposes.
